calibration.reason: Clear labels and legibility support the task, while the familiar layout limits originality and misplaced focus after invalid input harms recovery.

primary_action.input: Tab, then ArrowRight from the default 4 m radio
primary_action.expected: Select 6 m and show path, ferry and footbridge closures.
primary_action.observed: 6 m received visible focus; Riverside path was Closed, Ferry Stopped, and Footbridge Closed.

A-1440.edge_observation: Two ArrowLeft presses selected 2 m. Only the path had a closure label, but ferry and footbridge remained in the list without statuses.
A-1440.fact_check: The figure caption and selected marker say 6 m, and the shoreline advances compared with 4 m. Actual local closure thresholds and water levels were not independently verified.
A-1440.strength: A clear two-column composition pairs a legible result with an evocative shoreline illustration.
A-1440.weakness: Under a heading describing closures, unlabeled ferry and footbridge rows at 2 m make their status ambiguous.
A-1440.repair: Show only active closures, or explicitly label the other crossings as unaffected.

primary_action.expected: Select 6 m and show all three closure results.
primary_action.observed: All three results, the shoreline, and the 6 m caption were readable within the first 390 by 844 CSS-pixel viewport.

A-390.edge_observation: Two ArrowLeft presses selected 2 m; only the path had a closure label, while ferry and footbridge remained as unlabeled rows.
A-390.fact_check: The selected 6 m control, heading, marker and figure caption agree; the shoreline visibly changes from 4 m. Real-world conditions remain unverified.
A-390.strength: The stacked layout keeps the full result and illustration visible without scrolling.
A-390.weakness: The 2 m list includes crossings with no stated status under a closures heading.
A-390.repair: Filter the list to active closures or provide explicit unaffected statuses.

primary_action.expected: Select 6 m and show path, ferry and footbridge closures.
primary_action.observed: 6 m received visible focus and the list showed path Closed, ferry Stopped and footbridge Closed.

B-1440.edge_observation: Two ArrowLeft presses selected 2 m; the list contained only Riverside path Closed.
B-1440.fact_check: The caption and highlighted 6 m callout agree with the selected control and heading. The shoreline changes from 4 m, though its curved edge does not meet the 6 m marker uniformly. Actual local conditions were not independently verified.
B-1440.strength: Named callouts connect each threshold to its crossing, while the list contains only active closures.
B-1440.weakness: The stylized, curved shoreline makes the exact relationship between its edge and the selected marker somewhat difficult to read.
B-1440.repair: Clarify the marker-to-water relationship with a consistent reference line or short legend.

primary_action.expected: Select 6 m and show all three closure results.
primary_action.observed: All three closure rows, the labeled shoreline and the 6 m caption were readable within the first 390 by 844 CSS-pixel viewport.

B-390.edge_observation: Two ArrowLeft presses selected 2 m; the list contained only Riverside path Closed.
B-390.fact_check: The heading, selected radio, highlighted callout and figure caption all state 6 m; the shoreline changes from 4 m. Real-world conditions remain unverified.
B-390.strength: The complete result fits on screen and the callouts identify the crossings.
B-390.weakness: Callout boxes occupy much of the small illustration and obscure parts of the shoreline.
B-390.repair: Use a more compact mobile annotation arrangement while retaining the crossing names.

preference.reason: Both versions support the keyboard task and fit the complete 6 m result in the tested mobile viewport. B correctly limits the 2 m closure list to the path and connects thresholds to named crossings in the illustration, despite somewhat crowded mobile callouts.

experiment: Same frozen brief and exact shoreline parent. Targeted repair, distinct from a retrieval comparison.
